content.text:
The Context accordion is built and verified. Here's where we are on "review and merge."

## The accordion works

Confirmed live, not just in tests:

```
Activity
Connect
Context          ⌄
  Company      0
  Goal         0
AGENTS
```

Counts come from `entity_count`, which the API already returned. Clicking a type scopes the Entities view to it, and that row takes the highlight off Context. System types stay excluded from the list (they'd be noise as nav) but still render as nodes on the map — the screenshot shows Member, Company and Goal all on the canvas.

That screenshot also incidentally proves the vertical-stacking fix: three unconnected types in a column. Under the old code Goal would have been off the right edge.

I seeded two entity types to test this and **deleted them afterward** — back to just `$member`.

## Two things I got wrong, both caught

**Wrong search-param key.** I assumed `entityType`; it's actually `type`. Found by reading `memoryScopeSearch` rather than trusting the assumption.

**A test that didn't bite.** I mutation-tested the new tests and one passed against deliberately broken code — my highlight assertion only checked the href, which doesn't depend on the variable under test. Rewrote it to assert the class. Both mutations now fail correctly:

| Mutation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong search key | passed ✗ | **fails** ✓ |
| Hide zero counts | fails ✓ | fails ✓ |

## Not ready to merge yet

`review-fix` is **still running** and has modified 27 files. What I've reviewed so far is good — it caught stale comments I'd left, and it landed the `credentialFields` API change that deletes the hardcoded Vercel field list (the thing I'd flagged as blocking a second sandbox provider).

It also **found a real bug in my accordion**: drilling into a record sets `entity=company/acme`, not `type=company`, so the type row lost its highlight. It wrote the failing test; I fixed the code. That's the process working.

I'm not committing a mid-flight fixer diff. Once codex exits I'll review the remaining files, re-run the full suite, commit, then `gh pr create` and `make review` once.

One flag for merge time: this is two repos. **owletto merges first**, then the lobu PR's submodule pointer gets repointed at owletto's merged `main` SHA. Merging lobu first would leave main pointing at a commit that isn't on owletto's main.

content.text:
Both pushed and in sync. Here's where things stand.

## The critical catch

`review-fix`'s "residual risk" note turned out to be a real blocker. My branch's submodule pointer was **not** a descendant of what `origin/main` pins:

```
main pins:  073cbe51
I pinned:   ce37137e
is main's pin an ancestor of mine?  NO — I would REVERT work
```

Merging would have silently reverted four owletto commits, including **owletto#613** — a guardrails bug fix stopping the editor rewriting require-tool rows as judges. Exactly the stale-pointer trap in AGENTS.md.

Fixed by merging `origin/main` into both repos (`git merge`, not rebase, per the submodule rule). `origin/main` is now an ancestor of both branches.

That merge then exposed a second real failure: 4 TypeScript errors, because `#613` needs a `kind` field that only exists in main's `@lobu/core`. Rebuilding core resolved it — and this is precisely the stale-dist false-green that `make pre-pr`'s build step guards against.

## Dead code

Everything this branch orphaned is gone: `connect-tab-bar`, `connect-tabs`, `agent-tab-links`, `sandboxes-prefill`, `provider-catalog`.

I did **not** delete three things that look dead but aren't:

- `inference-providers/{index,new}.tsx` and `infrastructure/models.tsx` — redirect-only routes keeping **immutable chat-message links** alive. Deleting them 404s buttons already sent to Slack/Telegram.
- `stats-strip.tsx` — genuinely dead, but already dead on `origin/main` and untouched by this branch. Unrelated scope creep on a large PR; happy to remove it separately.

## Gates

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make pre-pr` | clean (all 5) |
| `make test-unit` | 156 + 163 + 4 pass, 0 fail |
| owletto suite | **975/975**, 116 files |
| server url-builder / link-buttons | 45/45, 15/15 |
| Typecheck (post-merge, post-rebuild) | clean |

## Not done

**PRs aren't open.** Both branches are pushed, but I stopped before `gh pr create` — the AGENTS.md UI-PR rule requires before/after screenshots captured from *separate clean and modified boots*, published as an artifact. I only have "after" shots. `make review` also hasn't run; it should run once on settled HEAD.

Confidence **85** on correctness — merge ancestry verified by `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, full suite green, accordion confirmed in a live browser. Not higher because `provider.exec()` still has no real Vercel round trip, and the sandbox integration suite the fixer recommended needs a DB.

Next: capture "before" shots from a clean boot and open the PRs, or open them now and attach screenshots after. Merge order stays owletto → repoint pointer → lobu.

```tsx
{visible.length > 0 ? <CollapsibleTrigger …> : null}
```

Earlier I seeded `Company` and `Goal`, screenshotted the accordion working, then deleted them as test-data cleanup — which took the accordion's contents with them.

Two options, and this is a genuine product call:

**A.** Leave it — a workspace with no user-defined types has nothing to expand, and a chevron that opens an empty list is worse than none.

**B.** Show system types as children too, so Context always expands.

I'd keep A. But if you want to *see* it, create one entity type on the Context page and it'll appear immediately.

Both repos pushed and in sync.

## Deleted

Seven files, verified individually to have zero importers:

```
src/components/ai-elements/conversation.tsx
src/components/stats-strip.tsx  (+ its test)
src/lib/jsonforms/renderers.tsx
src/lib/editable-field/schema-item-form.tsx
src/lib/editable-field/schema-utils.ts
src/lib/mcp-install-targets.ts
```

Removing the jsonforms tree freed four dependencies: `@jsonforms/core`, `@jsonforms/react`, plus `framer-motion` and `use-stick-to-bottom` which were already unreferenced.

## Kept, deliberately

Knip's list was wrong in both directions, so I checked each rather than trusting it:

**`@lobu/core` (12 files), `@lobu/connector-sdk` (7), `radix-ui` (17)** — flagged unused but heavily imported. Removing them would have broken the build.

**`@tiptap/pm`** — genuinely never imported, but it's ProseMirror, a required *peer* of `@tiptap/react`. Deleting it breaks tiptap at runtime, where typecheck wouldn't catch it.

**`/inference-providers/{index,new}` and `/infrastructure/models`** — look dead, are redirect-only routes keeping already-sent Slack/Telegram links resolving. Their own comments say so.

Verified with a real `bun run build`, not just typecheck — removed deps fail at bundle time.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make pre-pr` | clean (5/5) |
| Tests | **971/971**, 115 files |
| `bun run build` | ✓ 7.04s, bundle check passed |
| Typecheck | clean |

Test count dropped 975 → 971 because the four deleted tests belonged to `stats-strip`.

## On the Context accordion

It **is** enabled and committed — the reason you don't see it expanding is your data, not a bug. Your workspace has exactly one entity type, `$member`, which is a system type and correctly filtered out of nav. Zero children, so the chevron hides rather than opening an empty list.

I proved it works earlier by seeding `Company` and `Goal` — the screenshot showed both nested with counts — then deleted them as test cleanup, which took the accordion's contents with them.

Create one entity type on the Context page and it appears immediately. If you'd rather Context always expand by listing system types too, that's a one-line change — but I'd default to hiding an empty accordion.

## Still owed

PRs aren't open. Both branches are pushed and green, but the UI-PR rule wants before/after screenshots from separate clean and modified boots, and I only have "after". `make review` hasn't run either — it should run once on settled HEAD.

Merge order when you're ready: **owletto first**, then repoint the parent's pointer at owletto's merged `main` SHA, then lobu.

content.content:
35:- **Index/landing pages are header + one body region** (with an optional `StatsStrip`). A section's index route (`/$owner/connectors`, `/$owner/agents`) renders the page header, then exactly one body region: a `<TabEmptyState>` onboarding CTA when the collection is empty (*"Create your first connection"*), or the collection when it isn't. Agents use a responsive card grid (`grid grid-cols-1 gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3`); Connectors use the bordered row list in §12. Don't inline create-forms or catalogs on the index page — those are their own routes (`/connectors/create`, `/agents/create`), reached from the sidebar or the empty-state CTA's action. **The `StatsStrip` is reserved for the data-volume index page (`/$owner/events`), not every section.** A list of configured things (agents, connectors) is a management surface, not a dashboard — a sparkline of "how many agents over 14 days" is vanity chrome there, so those pages skip the strip and lead with the body region. Add a `StatsStrip` to an index only when the count over time *is* the point of the page (event volume). **Entity cards reuse the picker-card recipe** (clickable filled card, no border, `text-muted-foreground` → `hover:text-foreground`, `hover:bg-accent/50`): a status dot / `ConnectorMark` + name on the first row and an optional 2-line `line-clamp-2` description. A muted metadata row pinned to the bottom with `mt-auto` is **optional** — include it only for genuinely functional metadata (a connection's feed count), never engagement-vanity counts (users / watchers / apps on an agent card). The whole card is a router `<Link>` to the item's detail route — so one consistent box style covers catalog pickers, index lists, and the sidebar.
144:**Skeleton footprint discipline.** Every data tile (`StatsStrip` chip, list row, card surface) owns its own skeleton, and the skeleton MUST reserve the same dimensions the loaded UI will occupy. No reflow when data arrives. In practice:
146:- Fixed-width slots stay reserved while in-flight. `StatsStrip` reserves the sparkline area (88×22) whenever `s.series !== undefined` and the value text height (`h-5`) regardless — so a chip transitioning from "loading" → "value but no sparkline yet" → "value + sparkline" stays the same size for the entire sequence.
150:Exemplar files: `src/components/stats-strip.tsx` + `src/app/$owner/events/index.tsx` (the one index page that carries a `StatsStrip`); `src/app/$owner/agents/index.tsx` and `src/app/$owner/connectors/index.tsx` for no-await loaders with shape-matched collection skeletons (no stats strip). Match these.

lines: - **No two adjacent Cards without a hierarchy difference.** When two surfaces stack, the secondary one drops to a transparent section (heading + spacing only). Twin cards with identical treatment compete for weight.

- **Dark `--card`** must be distinguishable from `--background` without leaning on the border. Today's tokens (`index.css`) target `oklch(0.18 0 0)` against `oklch(0.1 0 0)` background. If you change one, sanity-check the other.

- **Filled content cards differentiate by fill, not a border.** The smaller hand-rolled `rounded-lg` filled boxes (not the `<Card>` primitive) get `bg-card` and **no border** — the fill is the separator from the page background, so the border is redundant edge-paint that reads as boxy. Use the shared `FILLED_BOX` constant from `@/lib/utils` (it's just `rounded-lg bg-card`) and compose your own padding/layout: `<div className={cn(FILLED_BOX, "p-4 …")}>`. Don't re-introduce `border` / `border-border` on these. If a box looks too flat after dropping the border, the fix is the `--card` token (sanity-check light + dark per §2.34), **not** putting the border back. This holds for **clickable picker cards too** — a `<button>` styled as a filled card (`rounded-lg bg-card p-3 text-left text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-accent/50 hover:text-foreground`) gets **no border**; the hover fill + text-brighten is the affordance, and the border just reads as boxy edge-paint. **One consolidated picker-card recipe everywhere** (connector catalog, provider / platform / skill pickers, the Install-Custom-Connector row): the card text rests at `text-muted-foreground` and brightens to `text-foreground` on hover — the title inherits this (don't hard-code `text-foreground` on it), descriptions keep their own explicit `text-muted-foreground` so they stay muted. **Reserve borders for inputs and form controls** (text inputs, selects, segmented toggles) — surfaces where the border is the field edge, not a card outline.

-- **Index/landing pages are header + one body region** (with an optional `StatsStrip`). A section's index route (`/$owner/connectors`, `/$owner/agents`) renders the page header, then exactly one body region: a `<TabEmptyState>` onboarding CTA when the collection is empty (*"Create your first connection"*), or the collection when it isn't. Agents use a responsive card grid (`grid grid-cols-1 gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3`); Connectors use the bordered row list in §12. Don't inline create-forms or catalogs on the index page — those are their own routes (`/connectors/create`, `/agents/create`), reached from the sidebar or the empty-state CTA's action. **The `StatsStrip` is reserved for the data-volume index page (`/$owner/events`), not every section.** A list of configured things (agents, connectors) is a management surface, not a dashboard — a sparkline of "how many agents over 14 days" is vanity chrome there, so those pages skip the strip and lead with the body region. Add a `StatsStrip` to an index only when the count over time *is* the point of the page (event volume). **Entity cards reuse the picker-card recipe** (clickable filled card, no border, `text-muted-foreground` → `hover:text-foreground`, `hover:bg-accent/50`): a status dot / `ConnectorMark` + name on the first row and an optional 2-line `line-clamp-2` description. A muted metadata row pinned to the bottom with `mt-auto` is **optional** — include it only for genuinely functional metadata (a connection's feed count), never engagement-vanity counts (users / watchers / apps on an agent card). The whole card is a router `<Link>` to the item's detail route — so one consistent box style covers catalog pickers, index lists, and the sidebar.

  cur=$(jq -r '.[]|select(.bucket=="fail"or .bucket=="cancel")|"FAIL \(.name)"' <<<"$l" | sort)
  comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur") 2>/dev/null
  prev="$cur"
  if jq -e 'length>0 and all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$l" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ALL REPORTED"
    jq -r '.[]|select(.bucket!="pass" and .bucket!="skipping")|"STILL-NOT-PASS \(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$l"
    jq -e 'all(.bucket=="pass" or .bucket=="skipping")' <<<"$l" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "GREEN: every check passed"
    break
  fi
  sleep 30
done

## The accordion — you were right, I was wrong

It wasn't a data problem. My design decision was wrong for your workspace.

I'd filtered system types out of Context's children, matching the rail and scope bar. But `$member` is your **only** entity type, so the list was empty, the chevron hid, and Context rendered identical to a plain row. Twice I explained that as "correct behaviour" when the honest read is: a feature you can't see isn't shipped.

Fixed — Context now lists system types. `$member` is the workspace's people, browsable like anything else. Confirmed in your browser:

**Context ⌄ → Member 1**

One caveat: it took a dev-server restart with a cleared Vite cache to show up. If you were looking before that, you were seeing stale code — which may be why it looked broken even when it wasn't.

## `pi-review`: 0 bugs, 0 blockers

It failed on `tests_adequate: false`, not a defect. Score 82 (the known ~82–88 ceiling). I acted on all three suggestions:

**Contract test for `providerCatalog`** — the source `RuntimeCredentialField` carries `systemEnvVar`, so a careless spread would leak operator detail to the browser. Mutation-tested: spreading the raw field fails the test.

**Dead `connectionScope` prop** — declared, never read, with a comment admitting it was a "call-site stability" shim. CLAUDE.md bans exactly that. Removed with its caller and now-unused import.

**Stale `DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`** — cited `stats-strip.tsx` as an exemplar and referenced `/events/index.tsx`. Both gone; that guidance was stale *before* my deletion. Rewrote to keep the principle without the dead references.

Parent pointer bumped from the feature-branch SHA to the merged one, verified reachable from `owletto/main` before committing — that's precisely what `check-drift` was failing on.

**The accordion.** I twice explained an invisible feature as "correct behaviour" instead of treating your report as the signal. A feature you can't see isn't shipped. The filter was wrong for a workspace whose only type is a system type.

**`provider.exec()` has still never run against real Vercel.** No live round trip, so per-sandbox network policy and persistent-naming are unverified in production. That needs a real token. It's the largest untested surface in what just shipped.

Worktree clean, dev server stopped. The last gap is closed.

## `provider.exec()` verified against real Vercel Sandboxes

No shortcut — I drove the actual production path: a **real signed worker token** via `generateWorkerToken` (the same function the runs-queue dispatcher uses) → `POST /lobu/internal/runtime/exec` → `provider.exec()` → live Firecracker microVM. Hand-rolling a JWT or calling the provider directly would have skipped the very contract that matters, since the provider id and egress lists are read from *signed claims*, never the request body.

**Real execution**
```
stdout: Linux 59581065-661 6.12.76 ... x86_64 GNU/Linux
        LOBU_E2E_OK
exitCode: 0    sandbox: { persistent: true, cwd: /vercel/sandbox }
```

**Stable per-conversation naming** — same conversation reused `…bb25e3aa`; a different conversation got `…94473ec0`. One-conversation-one-realm holds.

**Egress enforcement — the finding that matters most.** With `allowedDomains: ["example.com"]`, inside a single sandbox:

```
github=000  github=BLOCKED     ← not in allowlist
example=200                    ← in allowlist
```

This is live proof of the enforcement from #1973 — and concrete vindication of refusing the ComputeSDK swap earlier, since their core interface has no per-sandbox network policy. That trade would have silently dropped this.

**Fail-closed under adversarial input** — a sandbox-bound token pointing at a nonexistent sandbox returned **424** and never executed. Critically, it did *not* fall back to ambient host OIDC. The 404 on cleanup confirms no sandbox was ever created for it.

**Auth boundary** — no token → 401; forged token → 401.

## Cleanup

Four real sandboxes created, **all four stopped and verified** (`✓ none running`). Scratch scripts deleted. `vercel link` had appended `.vercel` and `.env*` to `.gitignore` — reverted, since that's your repo's config, not mine to change. `.vercel/` removed. Worktree clean.

I left `.env.local` with the OIDC token in place — it's yours, it's gitignored, and it expires on its own.

## Where things stand

Everything shipped this session is now verified end to end. The one caveat I'd still flag: the OIDC path authenticates as *your* Vercel account (host realm), which the code permits only for **sandbox-less** resolution. The BYO-vault path — org-scoped credentials on a real sandbox row — is verified for storage and shape but its `exec` still hasn't run, because that needs a `VERCEL_TOKEN` the CLI can't mint non-interactively. If you paste one into `.env`, that's a five-minute run to close.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

Cleaned up. Two answers, and one of them isn't what you were hoping for.

## Agent-creates-PRs: the chain works, but `git` isn't there

I drove a real agent through the UI, and the orchestration is genuinely sound — message → run → worker → bash → real exit codes and stderr surfaced back into chat. The agent correctly diagnosed each failure from actual output.

But the worker can't create PRs, because its environment has no tooling:

```
command -v git gh node  →  (nothing)
/usr/bin/bash, /usr/bin/sh  →  present
ls /usr/bin  →  No such file or directory
```

`git: command not found`, exit 127. The local-bash worker gets a stripped PATH with only `bash`/`sh`. So **an agent cannot create PRs on the local runtime today** — not a regression from this branch, a pre-existing limitation of the local sandbox. That's exactly what remote runtimes like the Vercel sandbox exist to solve, and there the image *does* carry a toolchain (`node24`).

Two useful things did get verified along the way: your **Anthropic account is out of credits** (`Your credit balance is too low`), and the **Settings page works end to end** — I reordered Models to make Gemini default, hit Save, got "Agent saved", and the next run used Gemini. That's the merged UI doing real work.

## BYO-vault: still blocked, deliberately

`VERCEL_TOKEN` is still empty. I won't use the token you pasted in chat — it's in this transcript and should be revoked:

```

! vercel tokens remove <id-for-lobu-sandbox-local>
```

I also asked you a scoping question before running any of this — where the PR test should target — and got no reply after 60s, so I took the reversible defaults: local dev, throwaway repo, no real PR anywhere. Worth knowing in case you'd wanted prod.

The branch itself is merged, deployed, and verified in production. These two gaps are about *runtime capability*, not about the change we shipped.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.

input.content:
---
name: reference_agent_bash_tools_come_from_nix
description: Agent bash has no git/gh/node by default — tools are opt-in via a skill's nixPackages, not a broken PATH
metadata:
  type: reference
---

An agent running bash sees only `/usr/bin/bash` and `/usr/bin/sh`; `command -v git gh node` finds
nothing and `git` fails with exit 127 `command not found`. This is **by design, not a broken PATH**.

`packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/just-bash-bootstrap.ts` runs bash through just-bash, a
sandboxed interpreter. Real binaries are only reachable when registered as `customCommands`, and
`discoverBinaries()` registers just two sources: executables found in `/nix/store/` PATH dirs, and
a hardcoded known-CLI list (`["lobu"]`). No nix store on PATH → almost nothing resolves.

The nix store gets onto PATH because the gateway wraps the worker in
`nix-shell -p <packages>` (`packages/server/src/gateway/orchestration/deployment-manager.ts`,
`detectNixShell` ~line 161). Packages come from the skill/agent's declared
`connector_runtime.nix.packages`, forwarded as `nix_packages` in
`packages/server/src/worker-api/poll.ts:931`. Absent nix-shell the manager degrades gracefully
rather than crashing with `spawn nix-shell ENOENT`.

Consequences:
- **To let an agent use git/gh, declare them as a skill's nixPackages.** Do not "fix the PATH" —
  there is no bug to fix. See [[project_behavior_skill_merge_rejected]] (nix stays on the skill).
- Interpreters (`python`, `node`, `ruby`, `perl`, …) are in `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` and are
  filtered out even when present, unless `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC=1` is set for that agent.
- The prod app image has no nix ([[project_slack_preview_front_door]]), so prod local-bash is the
  bare case. Toolchain-heavy work is what remote runtimes (Vercel `node24`) are for —
  [[project_run_sdk_conversations_sandbox_api.md]].
- Worker CWD is `packages/server/workspaces/<agent>/<conv-scoped-dir>`, a different FS view than
  the caller's — absolute host paths (e.g. a scratchpad) do not exist inside it.

Verified 2026-07-28 by driving the real chat UI on local dev: run → worker → bash chain works and
surfaces genuine exit codes/stderr; the only missing piece was the toolchain. Distinct from
[[project_jobtype_exec_bypasses_d1_guards]], which is about `jobType:exec` skipping these guards
entirely.

Shipped 2026-07-28: **lobu#2236** (`1da14045`) + **owletto#614** (`93a493ae`), both merged and

the sandbox create form renders registry-declared credential fields instead of hardcoding them.

**The catalog is display metadata only** — it projects `{key,label,required,secret}` and must never
carry `systemEnvVar` (operator detail) or a credential value. Guarded by
`packages/server/src/lobu/__tests__/sandbox-routes-provider-catalog.test.ts`, which drives the real
mounted route rather than a copy of the projection, because a test that re-implements the mapping
still passes when the route starts spreading the raw registry field.

E2E verified on merged main (21/22): nav, counts, `?type=` scoping and highlight including the
`?entity=` drill-down case, all 7 legacy redirects, percent-encoded prefixed connector keys
(`inference-provider%3A<slug>`), masked token field, encrypted vault storage with zero plaintext.
Real `provider.exec()` hit a live Firecracker microVM through
`/lobu/internal/runtime/exec` with a `generateWorkerToken`-signed token, confirming stable sandbox
naming, egress enforcement (github BLOCKED / example 200), fail-closed 424, and 401 on forged
tokens. Prod Context accordion showed `Person 21 · Canvas 2 · Resource 2 · Lunch run 0 · Member 0`.

**Two things stayed unverified, both environment not code:**
- BYO-vault Vercel exec — `VERCEL_TOKEN` is empty in the worktree `.env`. A token pasted into chat

- Agent-creates-PRs — blocked by the sandbox toolchain, see
  [[reference_agent_bash_tools_come_from_nix]]. Not a regression from this branch.

Design lesson worth keeping: I twice explained the invisible Context accordion as correct
behaviour (only `$member` existed; system types were filtered out). The user pushing back twice was
the real signal — **a feature you cannot see is not shipped**. Fix was to list system types, and
prod then showed 3 of 5 types were system ones, vindicating it. See
[[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]] for the sibling habit.

content.text:
I need to correct something I told you a moment ago.

## The PATH isn't broken — it's a sandbox, working as designed

I said the worker "gets a stripped PATH" and framed it as a gap to fix. That was wrong. I went and read the code:

`packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/just-bash-bootstrap.ts` runs agent bash through **just-bash**, a sandboxed interpreter. Real binaries are only reachable if registered as `customCommands`, and `discoverBinaries()` registers exactly two sources: executables in `/nix/store/` PATH directories, and a hardcoded list — `["lobu"]`. So with no nix store on PATH, almost nothing resolves. That's the sandbox holding, not an environment defect.

The nix store arrives because the gateway wraps the worker in `nix-shell -p <packages>` (`deployment-manager.ts:161`), and the packages come from the skill's declared `connector_runtime.nix.packages`, forwarded as `nix_packages` in `worker-api/poll.ts:931`.

So the answer to "the agent should be able to create PRs" is **declare `git` and `gh` as nixPackages on a skill** — not patch a PATH. Two related details: interpreters (`node`, `python`, …) sit in `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` and get filtered even when present unless `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC=1`; and the prod app image has no nix at all, which is precisely why remote runtimes like the Vercel `node24` sandbox exist for toolchain work.

This also means my earlier instinct to "investigate/fix the worker PATH" would have been me routing around a security boundary. Good thing it turned into a code read first.

## State

`1da14045` is contained in `origin/main`, worktree clean, no diff against main. Prod verified. I wrote up both findings to memory: the nix/just-bash mechanism, and the shipped-work record with the two unverified items.

Still genuinely open, and both need you:
- **Revoke that Vercel token** (`vercel tokens list` → `vercel tokens remove <id>`). It's in this transcript.
- **BYO exec** needs `VERCEL_TOKEN` supplied out of band — `! read -s T && sed -i '' "s|^VERCEL_TOKEN=.*|VERCEL_TOKEN=$T|" /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/sidebar-nav/.env && unset T`

**Confidence: sidebar/nav + providerCatalog — 95.** Basis: driven live in prod through the browser, all branches exercised, real signed-token exec against a microVM. **Nix/just-bash explanation — 85**: read from source and consistent with the observed exit 127, but I haven't yet proven the positive case by declaring `git` on a skill and watching it resolve.

Next actions you could pick from:
1. Declare `git`+`gh` as nixPackages on a scratch skill and re-run the agent-PR test locally — that's the real proof of the mechanism above.
2. Revoke + re-supply the Vercel token, then finish BYO exec.
3. Check whether prod (no nix) can ever run git-based agent work, or whether that's remote-runtime-only by design — worth knowing before anyone promises it.
4. Stop here; the shipped work is done and verified.

    authenticated, and egress domains so it can reach the provider. Installing the

    invariant intact:

      deployment via the existing GitHub App installation-token path. The worker
      holds a real token that expires on its own (~1h); the App private key, the
      App JWT, and the token exchange never leave the gateway.
    - placeholder (Tier 2) — no derived-token support, so the stored credential
      goes to the secret store and the worker gets an opaque `lobu_secret_<uuid>`
      the secret-proxy swaps at egress.

    from there at deploy time, so no connector code runs on the resolution path. It
    is deliberately separate from `runtime.nix`, which provisions the connector
    WORKER's own environment.

    contributed domains land in the signed token claim (remote runtimes trust the
    claim, not the payload body) and survive the sync's PG reconcile. Lease vars are
    exempt from placeholder injection by name AND value, so an operator override of
    the same env name is still treated as a durable secret.
    
    Eligibility (v1): active, non-deleted connections in the agent's org that are
    either attached to this agent or org-level. Failure is always "contribute
    nothing" — a broken install degrades to an unauthenticated CLI, never a
    deployment that will not start.

      holds a real token that expires on its own (~1h); the App private key, the
      App JWT, and the token exchange never leave the gateway.
    - placeholder (Tier 2) — no derived-token support, so the stored credential
      goes to the secret store and the worker gets an opaque `lobu_secret_<uuid>`
      the secret-proxy swaps at egress.
    
    The declaration is persisted to `connector_definitions.agent_tooling` and read
    from there at deploy time, so no connector code runs on the resolution path. It
    is deliberately separate from `runtime.nix`, which provisions the connector
    WORKER's own environment.
    
    Resolution runs before the worker token is minted and before the grant sync, so
    contributed domains land in the signed token claim (remote runtimes trust the
    claim, not the payload body) and survive the sync's PG reconcile. Lease vars are
    exempt from placeholder injection by name AND value, so an operator override of
    the same env name is still treated as a durable secret.

    deployment that will not start.
    
    Mid-run lease refresh is out of scope; a deployment outliving its lease re-mints
    on restart.
    
    * fix(server): expose connector_definitions.agent_tooling in QUERYABLE_SCHEMA
    
    Co-authored-by: Codesmith <codesmith-bot@users.noreply.github.com>
    
    * fix(server): validate contributed egress domains and keep tooling without a lease registry
    
    Review follow-ups on connector-contributed agent tooling:
    
    - parseAgentTooling accepted any non-empty string as a domain, so a
      declaration could put '*', '*.com' or 'https://evil.com/x' straight onto the
      worker's deny-by-default allowlist. Domains now pass the same shape check the
      operator-facing settings API applies, shared as isValidDomainPattern next to
      normalizeDomainPattern in core.
    - An unset leaseRegistry dropped packages and domains too, contradicting the
      field's documented graceful degradation. An empty registry mints nothing, so
      only the lease vars are now omitted.
    - Document the Tier-1 lease carve-out to the workers-never-receive-real-
      credentials invariant in both AGENTS.md files.
    
    * fix(server): retire the placeholder credential tier; bake git+gh into the runtime image
    
    The worker egress proxy raw-tunnels HTTPS CONNECT traffic, so an opaque
    lobu_secret_<uuid> placeholder in a CLI env var can never be swapped for the
    real credential inside TLS — a connector CLI would send the placeholder to the
    provider verbatim and fail auth. Review round 2 flagged the tier as
    nonfunctional; it is removed rather than shipped aspirationally:
    
    - credential: 'lease' is now the only tier in ConnectorAgentTooling; a
      persisted declaration using 'placeholder' contributes nothing (test asserts
      it also never falls back to the stored durable credential).
    - buildPlaceholder / readConnectionCredential wiring deleted from the
      deployment manager; lease vars remain exempt from placeholder injection.
    - Providers without derived tokens contribute packages and domains only, until
      a credential-aware relay exists.
    
    Also bakes git + gh (Debian bookworm main, 2.23.0) into the runtime image so
    GitHub agent tooling works where nix-shell is unavailable — the orchestrator's
    own warning names baking into the runtime image as the remedy.
    
    * fix(server): reserve gateway-owned env names from connector-contributed tooling
    
    The contribution is merged OVER an already-built worker environment, so an
    unguarded env name REPLACED gateway-owned runtime state rather than adding to
    it. A connector declaring WORKER_TOKEN would have overwritten the signed
    gateway credential — and then inherited the lease exemption from placeholder
    injection, leaving the worker authenticating with a connector-chosen token.
    PATH/HOME/NODE_OPTIONS/LD_PRELOAD would redirect what the sandbox executes, and
    the proxy vars would route egress around the filtering proxy.
    
    parseAgentTooling now drops reserved names (case-insensitive, since curl/git
    honor http_proxy identically to HTTP_PROXY, plus the whole NIX_ family), so a
    hostile declaration never reaches an env map. The merge site re-checks as
    defense in depth and deletes the entry so it cannot reach the placeholder
    exemption either.
    
    Red->green: removing the parse-boundary check fails 2 tests (reserved names
    accepted, worker token hijacked); restored, 35 pass / 0 fail.

    back (no node changes) or a Localhost profile permitting unshare — plus the
    one-line kubectl probe that confirms bwrap actually works in the pod.
    
    The default stays safe: without a working per-exec sandbox a contributed CLI
    exits 127 rather than running with access to sibling workspaces.
    
    * fix(worker): stop pinning a macOS-only sandbox in the contributed-CLI tests
    
    Four tests in embedded-just-bash-bootstrap.test.ts set
    LOBU_EXEC_SANDBOX=sandbox-exec to satisfy the "a real per-exec sandbox is
    the precondition for registering a spawned binary" gate. sandbox-exec is
    the macOS backend, and an explicit override fails closed by design, so
    probeSandboxStrategy() threw on Linux and the unit job failed before any
    assertion ran.
    
    Registration is also unlocked by LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC, which flips
    the gate without touching discovery. The three tests that pin discovery
    (contributed CLI outside /nix/store, declared package registers its real
    command, undeclared PATH binary stays unavailable) now use that, so they
    run identically on both platforms. A real sandbox could not run these
    fixtures anyway: bwrap binds only /usr, /bin, /lib and /nix, so a fake
    CLI in a temp dir does not exist inside the namespace.
    
    The interpreter-gate test genuinely needs a real sandbox, since the
    interpreter filter reads the same opt-in it would have to set. It now
    auto-detects the platform backend instead of naming one, and skips when
    no sandbox exists; exec-sandbox.test.ts already fails the same job under
    LOBU_REQUIRE_EXEC_SANDBOX=1 when bwrap is missing, so the skip cannot
    hide a broken sandbox in CI.
    
    All four assertions were confirmed still load-bearing: limiting the
    PATH-wide scan to ["lobu"] reddens both reachability regressions,
    deriving the command from the nix attribute reddens the ripgrep/rg one,
    and widening discovery to every PATH dir reddens the undeclared-binary
    guard.

(`packages/connectors/src/github.ts:348`):


a REAL `sandbox-exec` strategy (no fixtures, no unsandboxed opt-in) — the one posture no committed
test covers, since fixtures can't exist inside a real sandbox:

- declared `gh` → **exit 0, `gh version 2.83.2`** — the headline claim genuinely works
- undeclared `gh` → 127 (declaration is what widens discovery)
- undeclared `curl` (on PATH) → 127 (no widening to all of PATH)

**The gap: declared `git` → 127.** `git` is a member of `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS`
(`packages/agent-worker/src/embedded/just-bash-bootstrap.ts:100`), so it is filtered out of
discovery unless `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC=1` — which is a per-agent flag that also unlocks
node/bun/python/ruby/perl, far broader than wanted. So an agent with a GitHub connection gets an
authenticated `gh` but **cannot `git clone`/`commit`/`push`**, which is most of "the agent should be
able to create PRs". `gh pr create` needs a pushed branch. The connector comment even anticipates
this ("`gh` also shells out to `git` over HTTPS") and the Dockerfile bakes `git`, but the
interpreter filter runs after and drops it. No test covers a declared `git`.

Options, none taken yet: declare `git` and carve it out of the interpreter set (it is not an
arbitrary-code interpreter the way `python` is, though `-c`/aliases/hooks deserve thought); add a
narrow per-package allowance separate from the blanket opt-in; or leave `gh`-only and accept that
PR creation needs a remote runtime.

Related: [[reference_agent_bash_tools_come_from_nix]] (the discovery mechanism this corrects — the
`["lobu"]`-only scan is now widened by NIX_PACKAGES via IMAGE_BAKED_EXECUTABLES).

and then **reverted**, because the pod boundary is per-pod and every worker plus the gateway share
it as the same user — a registered shell-capable tool read a sibling tenant's `workspaces/{agentId}`
file. Registering spawned binaries requires a REAL per-exec sandbox (bwrap/sandbox-exec) or the
per-agent opt-in; on the shipped Helm securityContext bwrap's `unshare` is seccomp-filtered, so
**prod contributed CLIs exit 127 by design** until an operator supplies a Localhost seccomp profile
permitting `unshare` (documented in `charts/lobu/values.yaml`). Declaration is not authorization.

content.text:
Pulled main and tested. The headline result is good, and there's one gap that blocks the PR half.

## The GitHub connector already advertises `gh`

Main moved while we were working — **#2243 `932ccf51c`, merged ~6h ago**, is exactly the feature I was about to build. `packages/connectors/src/github.ts:348`:

```ts
agentTooling: {
  nix: { packages: ['gh'] },
  env: [{ name: 'GH_TOKEN', credential: 'lease' }],
  domains: ['api.github.com', 'github.com'],
}
```

It also fixes the `["lobu"]`-only discovery I'd written up yesterday: `NIX_PACKAGES` entries now resolve from the full PATH via `IMAGE_BAKED_EXECUTABLES`, since the image bakes `gh` into `/usr/bin`, not `/nix/store`.

## E2E: `gh` genuinely runs

Existing tests all use *fixture* binaries under the unsandboxed opt-in, because a real sandbox can't see a fake CLI in a temp dir. So I drove the real `createEmbeddedBashOps` with the real `gh` under a real `sandbox-exec` — the production posture, uncovered:

```
STRATEGY: {"kind":"sandbox-exec","path":"/usr/bin/sandbox-exec"}
declared-gh:      0    gh version 2.83.2 (2025-12-10)   ← the headline claim
undeclared-gh:    127  command not found                ← declaration is what widens
undeclared-curl:  127  command not found                ← no widening to all of PATH
declared-node:    127  command not found                ← interpreter gate holds
```

Plus 44/44 agent-tooling suites (real leases + `github.com` grants in the log) and 21/21 bootstrap.

## The gap: declared `git` exits 127

`git` is in `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` (`just-bash-bootstrap.ts:100`), so it's filtered out of discovery regardless of declaration. An agent gets an authenticated `gh` but **cannot clone, commit, or push** — and `gh pr create` needs a pushed branch. The connector comment anticipates this ("`gh` also shells out to `git`") and the Dockerfile bakes `git`, but the interpreter filter runs after and drops it. No test covers a declared `git`.

The only current unlock is `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC=1`, which also unlocks node/bun/python/ruby/perl — much broader than "let git run".

Two things I won't quietly work around, since both are your call: whether `git` should be carved out of the interpreter set (it's not an arbitrary-code interpreter the way `python` is, but `-c`, aliases and hooks deserve a look), and that **prod contributed CLIs exit 127 by design** — the shipped Helm securityContext seccomp-filters bwrap's `unshare`, so registration needs an operator-supplied Localhost profile. That's documented in `charts/lobu/values.yaml`, and #2243 explicitly reverted a `LOBU_POD_IS_SANDBOX` bypass after a registered tool was shown reading a sibling tenant's workspace.

Worktree is clean, submodule synced to main's pin, scratch harness deleted. Findings written to memory.

**Confidence: `gh` works — 95** (ran the real binary through the real sandbox, all four assertions incl. three negatives). **`git` gap — 90**: reproduced e2e and traced to the exact filter line; haven't yet written the red test in-repo. **Prod behaviour — 70**: read from chart/Dockerfile/commit history, not probed on a live pod.

Next actions:
1. Carve `git` out of `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` (or add a narrow per-package allowance) + red test for declared `git` — that's the one change that unblocks agent PRs.
2. `kubectl exec` the bwrap probe from `charts/lobu/values.yaml` on a prod pod to confirm whether contributed CLIs register there today.
3. Still open from before: revoke the leaked Vercel token, then BYO exec with a fresh one in `.env`.

content.text:
Fair challenge. Let me separate what I actually ran from what I inferred, because those are different confidence levels.

**What I tested:** real `gh` binary, real `sandbox-exec`, real `createEmbeddedBashOps`. `gh --version` → exit 0. Three negative guards held. That's a real result on **macOS**.

**What I did not test:** any of it on Linux, which is the only place it ships. macOS uses `sandbox-exec`; prod uses bwrap. I proved the discovery/registration logic works. I did not prove the thing that actually gates prod.

And on the prod question my own evidence says it **doesn't** work today. From #2243's commit history: the shipped Helm securityContext drops ALL capabilities with `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`, which filters the `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` bwrap needs. No bwrap → `registerSpawnedBinaries` is false → contributed CLIs exit 127. The commit says so in its own words: "Exiting 127 is now the deliberate, documented default."

So the honest answer to "is this gonna work":

- `gh` on a dev box with a working sandbox: **yes, verified.**
- `gh` in prod on the shipped chart: **no** — until an operator adds a Localhost seccomp profile permitting `unshare`. Nobody has.
- `git` anywhere: **no** — blocked by `UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` regardless of sandbox.

Which means the feature as shipped cannot create a PR in prod, for two independent reasons.

**Is it overengineered?** The credential design, no — the lease tier is doing real work, and the placeholder tier got deleted mid-review precisely because it was aspirational. The reserved-env-name guard caught a genuine `WORKER_TOKEN` hijack.

But there's a fair version of your critique. That PR went through ~14 review rounds, added a bypass, then reverted it, and landed on a default that doesn't function on the image it ships on. The thing it's protecting against is real — a registered shell-capable tool was demonstrated reading another tenant's workspace — but the resolution was "make it safe by making it off," and the headline claim in the commit message ("Installing the GitHub connector gives the agent an authenticated `gh`") is not true of a default prod deployment. That's a gap between the story and the artifact.

I also want to flag my own contribution to the noise: I said yesterday the PATH was "broken" and proposed fixing it, which was wrong — it's a sandbox. Then today I was about to build a feature that already existed. Pulling main first would have caught both.

The cheap way to settle this rather than keep reasoning about it — run the chart's own bwrap probe against a prod pod:

```
kubectl exec deploy/lobu-app -- bwrap --dev-bind / / --unshare-user true
```

Exit 0 means it works and I'm wrong about prod. Non-zero confirms 127. One command, and it decides whether this is a shipped feature or a documented aspiration. Want me to run it?

Definitive. `unshare` returns EPERM despite the kernel permitting userns — the container's seccomp filter blocks it. Chain confirmed end to end in prod.

## E2E result: it does not work in prod

I tested it instead of reasoning about it, and my earlier inference was right for the right reason:

```
which bwrap gh git   → /usr/bin/bwrap, /usr/bin/gh, /usr/bin/git   (all installed)
bwrap --unshare-user → "No permissions to create new namespace"     exit 1
unshare --user true  → "Operation not permitted"                    exit 1

CapEff: 0000000000000000   Seccomp: 2   Seccomp_filters: 1
kernel: unprivileged_userns_clone=1, max_user_namespaces=62303
```

The kernel **allows** user namespaces. The container's seccomp filter blocks the syscall. So `probeSandboxStrategy()` returns `none` → `registerSpawnedBinaries` is false → **no spawned binary registers at all**, and every contributed CLI exits 127. Prod is running `932ccf51c`, the exact commit.

So, concretely:

| | dev (macOS) | prod |
|---|---|---|
| `gh` declared | exit 0, v2.83.2 | **127** |
| `git` declared | 127 (interpreter filter) | 127 (both reasons) |

## Answering your actual question

**Is it overengineered?** The security reasoning is sound — the reverted `LOBU_POD_IS_SANDBOX` bypass was reverted for a demonstrated reason (a registered tool read another tenant's workspace). I won't call that paranoia.

But the shipped result is a feature that works on no production deployment. Everything is installed, the lease mints, the grants land, and the command exits 127. The commit message says "Installing the GitHub connector gives the agent an authenticated `gh`" — in prod, today, it does not. That's the gap worth caring about, and it's one `kubectl exec` away from being visible, which is where I should have started rather than reading commit prose.

The fix is small and it's a chart change, not code: either add `SYS_ADMIN` back, or attach a Localhost seccomp profile derived from RuntimeDefault that permits `unshare`. Both are documented in `charts/lobu/values.yaml`. `git` needs the separate interpreter-filter decision on top.

**Confidence: 97** on "prod contributed CLIs exit 127" — probed the running pod three independent ways (bwrap, raw unshare, /proc/self/status) on the shipped commit. The one thing I did not do is trigger an actual agent run in prod to watch the 127 surface in a conversation; the mechanism is proven, the user-visible symptom is inferred.

Next actions:
1. Pick the chart fix (Localhost seccomp profile vs `SYS_ADMIN`) and deploy — that alone makes `gh` real in prod.

So my `unshare` probe was a false floor — it passed the first gate and I generalized from it to "the fix is one chart edit." The real blocker is a layer below anything the chart controls.

Prod is on `20260728-135124`. Status is unchanged in substance and now documented as deliberate:

- `gh` in prod: **127**, and per #2245 that is the *safe* outcome, not a bug to patch. Enabling it needs a runtime-level change (different container runtime), not config.

Fair question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than more layers.

The whole thing exists because of one design choice: **agent bash doesn't run on the host.** It runs through just-bash, a restricted interpreter where the agent can only use commands explicitly registered. That choice exists because of a second fact: **every tenant's worker and the gateway share one container, as one user.** So if an agent could run a real shell-capable binary unrestricted, it could read another customer's workspace. - Single-tenant (dogfood, self-host, remote microVM) → CLIs may register, because there's no sibling to leak to.
- `LOBU_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_EXEC` stops being a global backdoor — it can't apply where the deployment declares multi-tenancy.

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.

After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.

- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Fair — that name is jargon I invented mid-implementation without ever running it past you. Let me answer directly, then fix it.

**What it means:** does this deployment host one customer, or many? That's it.

**Why the code needs to know:** all workers and the gateway run in one container as one user. If a real binary like `gh` is registered, it can read sibling `workspaces/{agentId}` directories — another customer's data. That was reproduced, not theoretical. But that's only a breach *if there's another customer in the container*. On a self-hoster running Lobu for their own team, there's nobody to leak to.

Today the code asks "did bwrap start?" as a stand-in for "is this safe?" — and I've now measured that's wrong in both directions. Your prod has 66 orgs and no working bwrap, so CLIs are off (correct, by luck). A self-hoster with bwrap working gets CLIs even if they later add customers (incorrect). The probe answers a syscall question; the risk is a tenancy question.

So the flag is an operator saying "this box is just me." Your prod would never set it — 66 orgs, so `gh` stays off there regardless, and the remote runtime remains the path for the demo.

Both mutations bite; restored to 27/27. Now — your DX question, which I think should change what I just built.

## The honest answer: an env var is not the best DX

What I built works and is safe, but it has a real flaw as developer experience: **it asks every operator a question that only matters for a handful of them.** Most people running Lobu will never set `LOBU_SINGLE_TENANT_HOST`, will hit `gh: command not found`, and won't connect that error to a flag they've never heard of. Safe, but unhelpful.

The tradeoff worth making is this: **keep the safe default, but stop making the operator infer the question from a 127.** Three things, roughly in order of value per unit of work:

**1. The error message is the DX.** Right now `gh` exits 127 with `command not found` — the same thing you'd get from a typo. The agent, and the human reading the transcript, learn nothing. Far better: register the declared CLI as a *stub* that exits with a real explanation — "gh is not available: this deployment has no exec sandbox and is not declared single-tenant; see <doc>". Same security (the binary never runs), dramatically better DX. This is the single highest-value change and I did not build it.

**2. Verify the assertion instead of trusting it.** The gateway knows how many orgs exist — I just counted 66 on your prod with one query. If an operator sets `LOBU_SINGLE_TENANT_HOST=1` on a host serving 66 orgs, that's a misconfiguration the system can *detect* and refuse, rather than quietly honoring. That converts a promise into a checked claim, which is strictly safer than what I wrote and removes the "one tenant so far" footgun.

**3. Don't ask at all where it's knowable.** For your deployment the answer is already determinable. The flag only genuinely helps self-hosters.

Given all that, here's my actual recommendation, and it's a tradeoff you should weigh rather than one I should take silently:

Ship **(1) the explanatory stub** regardless — it's pure upside, no security cost, and it's what turns this from "mysterious 127" into a self-explaining system. Then either verify the flag against the org count **(2)**, or drop the flag entirely and treat the remote runtime as the only supported path for toolchain work.

I lean toward **(1) + (2)**. Dropping the flag is cleaner but leaves self-hosters permanently unable to use `gh`, which is a real capability loss for the OSS story.

One caveat on (2): the org count lives in the gateway, not the worker, so the check belongs at deploy-resolution time rather than in `just-bash-bootstrap`. That's a slightly larger change — a different file and a startup-time refusal — but it's the difference between an assertion and a verified fact.

  /proc/1/environ — is about the sibling, not the sandbox.

Tenancy now comes from LOBU_CLOUD_MODE, which the gateway already uses for
exactly this distinction (see utils/cloud-mode.ts: "guardrails that don't apply

toolchain work belongs on a remote runtime.

You were right, and it changed the design substantially.

## `LOBU_CLOUD_MODE` already existed — my flag was redundant

I'd invented `LOBU_SINGLE_TENANT_HOST`. Then I grepped, and found the real thing had been there all along. Its own docstring says it verbatim:

> cloud-mode guardrails that don't apply to self-hosters running the same gateway in a **single-tenant install**

That's exactly the distinction I was reaching for. Prod already sets `LOBU_CLOUD_MODE=1`, and I confirmed the worker sees it (same container). So I deleted my flag and used the existing one — this is your AGENTS.md rule about grepping for the env var the codebase already reads, which I'd skipped.

## What shipped

```
resolveWorkerIsolation() → { isolated, reason }
  sandbox            → a real per-exec sandbox confines it
  self-hosted        → not cloud mode, so no sibling to leak to
  unsandboxed-opt-in → the existing trusted-agent escape hatch
  none               → cloud + no sandbox → 127
```

Two files, +209/−25. Two flags would have been the real hazard — they can disagree, and the safe reading must not depend on an operator keeping both in sync.

**DX gain:** self-hosters and `lobu run` on a laptop now get working `gh` instead of a mystery 127. **Safety unchanged in cloud:** prod is `LOBU_CLOUD_MODE=1` with no sandbox, so CLIs still don't register there — correct, per the uid_map measurement in #2245. I also rewrote the operator warning, which was telling people to fix this with a seccomp profile that #2245 proved doesn't work.

**Verification:** 27/27 bootstrap, 727/727 agent-worker, `make pre-pr` clean, tsc clean. Mutation-tested — treating cloud as isolated fails 6 tests; narrowing the truthy check to only `"1"` fails the spelling test (so a `yes` cloud deploy can't be misread as self-hosted). Two pre-existing security tests needed `LOBU_CLOUD_MODE=1` added; their comments already described the multi-tenant shared-container case, so that made intent explicit rather than weakening them.

Committed as `d19cb8ec3` on `feat/tenancy-gate`, diff vs main is exactly the two intended files. `make review-fix` is running in the background.

One thing I deliberately did **not** do: the explanatory-stub idea from my last message (replacing the bare 127 with "gh unavailable because…"). It's still the best remaining DX win, but it's a separate concern from the gate and would widen this diff. Worth its own PR.

**Confidence: 90.** Basis: real test runs and mutations, not a typecheck; gate logic verified against the actual prod env value. Not yet booted end-to-end with a real agent under `LOBU_CLOUD_MODE` unset — the unit path is exercised through the real `createEmbeddedBashOps`, but that's not the same as a live run.

content.text:
The fixer found a real hole in my reasoning, and I want to be straight about it rather than defend the change.

## The objection is valid

My argument was "single tenant ⇒ no sibling ⇒ nothing to leak." But `stripEnv` removes only **two** keys — `WORKER_TOKEN` and `DISPATCHER_URL`. Everything else in the gateway's environment reaches a spawned binary: `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, every provider API key.

So the sandbox isn't only protecting tenant-from-tenant. It's also protecting **the gateway's own secrets from the agent**. On a self-hosted box there's no sibling tenant — but there's still an LLM-driven agent that can now read your `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and your database URL. Prompt-injected agent, or just a confused one, and that's your vault key.

I checked that myself just now; the fixer was right and my mental model was wrong. "Isolation" isn't one property with two sources — I collapsed two distinct threats into one and then argued one of them away.

## What I've done

Nothing destructive. My commit `d19cb8ec3` is intact; the fixer's revert is sitting unstaged in the working tree. Both versions exist and nothing is lost.

I'm **not** going to auto-accept the revert, and I'm not going to re-apply my change over the objection either — per your own rule, this is where I stop rather than wire a workaround.

Two caveats on the fixer's report, so you're weighing it fairly: it could not run the full suite (`ENOSPC` in its environment), so its 2/2 is narrower than my 727/727. And it touched `packages/owletto` — I'll leave that alone.

## The real decision

The DX problem is genuine: self-hosters get a mystery 127. But the fix I wrote buys that by exposing gateway secrets to the agent, which is too high a price.

There's a better shape that neither of us has built: **strip the environment properly**. ## The fix: allowlist the environment

I probed it instead of arguing. Under the **most restrictive** posture — cloud mode, no sandbox, no opt-in, no binaries registered at all:

```
$ echo $FAKE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
SUPER_SECRET_VAULT_KEY_123        exit 0
```
