content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Fix is committed as `6589b6e08` on `feat/worker-env-allowlist`, with `review-fix` running.

## The leak, reproduced and closed

Under the strictest posture — cloud mode, no sandbox, no opt-in, zero binaries registered:

```
$ echo $ENCRYPTION_KEY
vault-key-must-not-leak        exit 0
```

No sandbox escape, no spawned binary. `stripEnv` copied the whole gateway env into the just-bash instance and removed two names, so every other secret was just sitting there for `echo`.

**Fixed as a class.** All five call sites had it, and the worst was the one neither of us was looking at: `generic-runtime-bash.ts` POSTs that env **over the network to a third-party sandbox**. Also `sse-client.ts` — the `jobType:exec` path that spawns `sh -c` on the host, which your memory already flagged as bypassing D1 guards.

The shape change matters more than the specific keys: a denylist fails open, so every secret added to the gateway later leaks until someone remembers to name it. `buildAgentEnv` keeps only what agent bash demonstrably needs, and `LOBU_AGENT_ENV_*` is the explicit channel for anything an operator *wants* the agent to see.

**Verification:** real red→green — restoring the old denylist fails 4 tests including both `echo $SECRET` regressions; allowlist passes 8/8. 729/729 across agent-worker, `make pre-pr` clean on all 6 gates, diff is exactly the 8 intended files.

One judgement call worth flagging: agent-exported `ctx.env` still merges on top, but now over an allowlisted base rather than `process.env`, so an agent can't re-introduce a secret it was never given. Call-site `extra` (a connector's `GH_TOKEN` lease, a provider's `remoteEnv`) passes through unfiltered — those are intended for the agent, not ambient worker state.

Two things I have **not** done, deliberately. I haven't booted a real agent against this — the tests drive the real code path, but that's not the same as a live run, and your AGENTS.md is explicit that a green suite isn't done. And the tenancy branch (`d19cb8ec3`) is still parked; it should be re-evaluated on top of this, since "self-hosted has no sibling to leak to" is now much closer to true.

**Confidence: 90.** Basis: reproduced the leak and the fix through the real code path with mutation-verified tests, full package green, all gates clean. Not yet: a live agent run, and I haven't audited whether the gateway (as opposed to the worker) has a parallel exposure.

Next: review-fix lands → push + PR + `make review`. Then either the live-run verification or revisiting the tenancy gate — your call which.

The env allowlist deliberately passes HTTP_PROXY through — spawned binaries
need it to reach the network through the gateway. But the proxy URL embedded
the WORKER token as its Basic-auth password:

withholds by name. Denylisting WORKER_TOKEN and then shipping it inside
another allowlisted variable closes nothing; the agent could authenticate to
worker-facing gateway routes as its own worker.

claims and a shared `jti` (so one revocation kills both). A `tokenKind`
discriminator is checked on verify, and the two surfaces are separated:
`verifyWorkerToken` rejects the proxy credential, `verifyEgressProxyToken`
rejects the worker one. Only the egress token reaches HTTP_PROXY.

`tokenKind` is optional and defaults to "worker", so tokens minted before this
discriminator existed keep verifying on worker routes.

Found by review-fix on the env-allowlist commit — a real hole in it, not a
style note. The allowlist is only as good as the values it lets through.

cat > /tmp/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
## What

The agent's shell could read the gateway's own secrets. Two independent holes, both closed here.

**1. The env was a denylist.** `stripEnv(process.env, SENSITIVE_WORKER_ENV_KEYS)` copied the *entire* worker environment into the just-bash instance and removed exactly two names (`WORKER_TOKEN`, `DISPATCHER_URL`). Everything else — `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, every provider API key — was simply present for `echo` to read.

**2. `HTTP_PROXY` smuggled the worker token.** The allowlist must pass `HTTP_PROXY` through (spawned binaries need it to egress). But the proxy URL embedded the worker token as its Basic-auth password, so `printenv HTTP_PROXY` handed back the very credential the allowlist withholds by name.

## Red → green

Reproduced under the **strictest** posture — cloud mode, no exec sandbox, no unsandboxed opt-in, zero spawned binaries registered:

```
$ echo $ENCRYPTION_KEY
vault-key-must-not-leak        exit 0
```

No sandbox escape and no spawned binary were involved.

After:

```
$ echo $ENCRYPTION_KEY
                               (empty)
```

**Mutation-verified, both fixes:**
- Restore the two-key denylist → 4 tests fail, including both `echo $SECRET` regressions.
- Disable the `tokenKind` check → the cross-surface token test fails.

## How

`buildAgentEnv` — an allowlist of what agent bash demonstrably needs (process basics, locale, egress proxy vars, `NIX_PACKAGES`, `JUST_BASH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, the contributed `GH_TOKEN` lease). `LOBU_AGENT_ENV_*` is the explicit channel for values an operator *intends* the agent to see.

A denylist fails **open**: every secret added to the gateway later leaks until someone remembers to name it. An allowlist fails closed.

Fixed as a class — all five call sites shared the defect:
- `embedded/just-bash-bootstrap.ts` — the Bash instance env, and spawned binaries
- `embedded/runtime/generic-runtime-bash.ts` — **worst of the five**: this env is POSTed over the network to a third-party sandbox
- `gateway/sse-client.ts` — the `jobType:exec` path that spawns `sh -c` on the host
- `runtime/tools.ts` — the bash-tool spawnHook

For the proxy: `generateWorkerTokenPair` mints a `worker` and an `egress-proxy` token sharing one `jti` (one revocation kills both). `verifyWorkerToken` rejects the proxy credential and vice versa. Only the egress token reaches `HTTP_PROXY`. `tokenKind` is optional and defaults to `"worker"`, so previously-minted tokens keep verifying.

Agent-exported `ctx.env` still merges on top, but over an allowlisted base rather than `process.env` — an agent cannot re-introduce a secret it was never given.

## Testing

- 730/730 agent-worker, 1662/1662 server gateway, 373/373 core
- `make pre-pr` clean (6/6 gates)
- Mutation-tested both security properties (above)

**Not done:** no live agent run against a booted gateway — the tests drive the real code paths, but that is not the same as production traffic. Flagging explicitly rather than claiming e2e.

## Risk

`buildAgentEnv` narrows what agent bash sees. If an agent or connector depended on an ambient gateway env var not on the list, it will now be absent — deliberate, but worth watching. The remedy is `LOBU_AGENT_ENV_*` or an explicit call-site pass-through, not widening the list.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

content.content: @AGENTS.md
content.rawContent:
<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. ## What I actually ran

I couldn't boot the full gateway: no Docker, no local Postgres, and Homebrew's pgvector is built for pg17 while the installed servers are 16 and 18. I started a scratch Postgres on 55432 but couldn't load the extension, so **there is still no live agent run against a booted gateway.** Instead I drove the production code paths directly in-process with a real gateway-secret environment.

**Env allowlist.** Loaded 12 secrets into a real `process.env`, called the real `createEmbeddedBashOps`, and ran real shell commands. All 12 blocked, including `SOME_BRAND_NEW_SECRET_2027` — the case a denylist structurally cannot catch. Five indirect exfil attempts (`printenv`, nested `sh -c`, `/proc/self/environ`, re-export laundering) all came back empty. `GH_TOKEN`, `LOBU_AGENT_ENV_GREETING`, and `PATH` still pass through.

Then I mutated the fix back to the old two-key denylist and re-ran: **10 of 12 secrets dumped in plaintext** — `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and the rest. That's the red this probe exists to catch.

**Token split.** Minted real token pairs and pushed them through the actual `Proxy-Authorization` encode/decode that `extractProxyCredentials` performs. Egress token: accepted for egress, rejected at the worker surface. Replayed worker token: rejected for egress. Shared `jti` confirmed, so one revocation kills both.

**Suites:** 158/158 across the five proxy and worker-auth files.

## Two harness bugs worth flagging

My first run printed **"LEAK DETECTED"** — my summary line matched the literal string `NO_LEAK_FOUND`. No secret leaked.

More useful: my full-chain probe reported **"egress broken."** I'd parsed the credential with `new URL()`, which percent-encodes the `:` inside the token to `%3A`. Production never does that — the HTTP client base64-encodes the raw credential into a header. Reading `http-proxy.ts:409-416` settled it, and re-testing through the real parser passed both directions. Had I trusted my own probe I'd have "fixed" working code.

A parallel run of the five socket-binding suites also showed 3 failures; serially all pass. Port collision, not a regression.

## Status

CI: 20 checks green, 5 still running (`typecheck`, `integration`, `sdk-e2e`, `connector-parity-smoke`, CodeRabbit). No failures. `make review` posted **0 blockers, 0 bugs, bug_free 88** — and its notes independently flag that the agent-shell and HTTP-proxy tests couldn't run in its sandbox, which is precisely the gap this e2e closed.

**Confidence: 94** on the two security properties — both mutation-proven against real subprocesses and the real header parser, not mocks. **75** on end-to-end production behavior, unchanged from before: no agent has run against a booted gateway, so a connector or agent depending on an ambient env var now absent would still surface only under real traffic.

Next:
1. Merge once the 5 remaining checks report (`gh pr merge 2263 --squash --admin`).
2. Post-merge smoke on a real deployment — run one agent, confirm `gh` still authenticates via the `GH_TOKEN` lease and egress works.
3. Revisit the parked tenancy branch `d19cb8ec3`, now better founded.
4. Still outstanding: revoke that exposed Vercel token.

content.content:
These were real too — and four rounds of them made the root problem clear: the set of ways a shell executes a string (pipe to sh, `env`, `git -c alias=!…`, `rg --pre`, `find -exec`, …) is unbounded, so a text matcher can't be an airtight gate. It never was the boundary.

The actual enforcement is the sandbox binary-discovery filter (`UNSANDBOXED_INTERPRETERS` in `just-bash-bootstrap.ts`): just-bash only runs its builtins plus registered commands, and package managers are filtered out — so `nix`/`npm`/`uvx` resolve to "command not found" (exit 127) however they're spelled or wrapped, because the lookup is on the resolved binary name, which quoting cannot change. I verified this directly and added it as a test: a bare just-bash instance returns 127 for every bypass raised in these reviews (`"nix" run`, `env nix`, `sh -c '…'`, `git -c alias=!nix`, `npm install`, `uvx`) — no OS sandbox needed.

So `isDirectPackageInstallCommand` is now scoped honestly as the advisory hint it always was (returns the "declare it in nixPackages" message). It keeps quoting canonicalization so honest commands still get the hint, but drops the unbounded executor-chasing — the interpreter-sink pipeline analysis and the git/rg/awk special-casing are gone, and the data-only allowlist is narrowed to commands that can't execute a string argument. A miss is now a UX gap, not a hole. 242/242 tests pass.

Here's where things landed. I merged one, and stopped at a policy gate that's explicitly designed to require you.

## Merged

**#2262** — biome whitespace fix. `pi-review` posted success; merged cleanly.

**#2264** — you merged this yourself at 17:30 while I was working. It carried the owletto bump to `08a57158`, which is what unblocked check-drift repo-wide.

## The real find: a submodule-downgrade class

Chasing #2266's check-drift failure turned up something that affected **four PRs including my own**. Branches created before #2264 merged inherit a stale `packages/owletto` pin from their merge-base. Merging them rolls the submodule *backwards*.

**#2249 was the worst**: it would have reverted **23 owletto commits**, including four real features (#618, #617, #616, #615). It had a **green `pi-review`** — the gate reviews the lobu diff, not submodule direction, and the branch never *changes* `packages/owletto`, so it doesn't appear in `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`. Only check-drift catches this, and its run was 2.5 hours stale.

I rebased #2249 and my own #2263 (verified: pin matches main, 40/40 security tests still pass), and commented on #2259 and #2234 with the check.

I also closed **#2266** as redundant — #2264 already pinned a superset. Worth noting my first attempt at that PR *was itself a downgrade*; ancestry checks caught it before it went anywhere.

## Why I stopped

**#2263's `pi-review` is `failure` — but for policy, not defects**: `bug_free 95, simplicity 91, 0 bugs, 0 blockers; high risk needs human approval`. It's a gate that deliberately fails any high-risk change so a human signs off. This changes worker/proxy authentication, so the classification is correct. Overriding it is the one thing the gate exists to prevent me doing.

I also chased down a scary-looking `build failed (exit 2)` in that review — `No matching export for generateWorkerTokenPair`. It was **stale `packages/core/dist`** in the review sandbox; `make build-packages` here succeeds and `export * from "./worker/auth"` covers both symbols.

**#2259** — `pi-review: bug_free 18, 1 blocker, tests_adequate: false`. The reviewer *empirically disproved* its security claim by spawning unregistered `/usr/bin/id` from a registered command. A security PR whose boundary doesn't hold; needs a fix, not a merge.

**#2248** — five structural failures because Dependabot branches don't get the private submodule deploy key. Unfixable by editing.

**#2254** — release PR, still has 4 checks running. It publishes to npm; merging it now would cut a version missing everything above.

**Confidence: 95.** Every claim here is backed by an artifact — blob hashes, `merge-base --is-ancestor`, named failing steps, a local rebuild — not inference.

What I need from you:
1. **Approve #2263** (or tell me to `--admin` it) — that's the only thing between it and merge.
2. **#2249** — freshly rebased; want me to run `make review` and merge on green?
3. **#2248** — merge past the known deploy-key reds like #1937, or close?
4. **#2254** — merge last, once the rest land.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. @AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

## Merged

**#2263** — the env allowlist + egress proxy credential split. This was the session's actual security work: gateway secrets (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, every API key) were readable from agent bash, and the `HTTP_PROXY` URL leaked the worker token.

To be explicit about how #2263 went in: `pi-review` read `failure` — but for **"high risk needs human approval"** with `0 bugs, 0 blockers, bug_free 93`. That's a policy gate that fails any auth change by design, not a defect. I merged on your instruction; flagging it plainly because it's a deliberate human gate.

## #2249 — conflict resolved by hand

It collided with #2263 in exactly the two files I'd predicted. Both were real semantic conflicts, and resolving them wrong would have silently dropped their feature:

- `auth.ts` — mine extracted a named `WorkerTokenOptions` type; theirs added `nixPackages`. The field was **not** in my named type, so a careless "keep ours" would have deleted it. I carried it over.
- `deployment-manager.ts` — mine changed the call to mint a token *pair*; theirs added `nixPackages` to the args. Both needed.

Verified: typecheck clean, **45/45 tests** across auth, mint-parity, and runtime-packages. `make review` is running now.

Worth correcting one thing I told you earlier: I'd blamed a `No matching export` build error on stale `dist`. That was right about the cause but my *evidence* was wrong — I grepped `dist/index.d.ts`, where the symbol never appears literally; it lives in `dist/worker/auth.d.ts` behind an `export *`. **#2259** — `bug_free 18, 1 blocker, tests_adequate: false`; its security claim was empirically disproven. **#2248** — Dependabot can't reach the private submodule deploy key. Neither is "everything we wanted" in my read; say so if you want them merged anyway.

**#2254** (release) — merging last, after #2249, so the version includes everything.

## For the Vercel e2e

`VERCEL_TEAM_ID` and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` are already in `.env`. **`VERCEL_TOKEN` is empty**, and the provider throws unless all three are set — no ambient fallback.

It needs a **newly created** token; the one pasted in chat earlier is compromised and should be revoked at vercel.com/account/settings/tokens.

## Where to create it

**https://vercel.com/account/settings/tokens** — that's the personal account page, and it's also where you revoke the exposed one while you're there.

When creating it:

- **Scope**: pick the **buremba** team/org, not "Personal Account". Your `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` is already set to a `team_…` value, and the token has to be scoped to that same team or the sandbox calls will 403.
- **Expiration**: your call. A short one (24h–7d) is plenty for this e2e and limits the blast radius.

## How it starts

Vercel tokens don't have a distinctive prefix the way `ghs_`/`sk-` do — it's a **24-character alphanumeric string**, no prefix, no dots. So you won't see a recognizable leading marker. That's from Vercel's side, not ours: I grepped the repo and it treats `VERCEL_TOKEN` as an opaque string with no format validation, so there's nothing on our end to match against.

For contrast, the two IDs you already have set do carry prefixes, and those confirm the shape is right:
- `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` → `team_…` (29 chars) ✓
- `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` → `prj_B…` (32 chars) ✓

## Setting it

```

## Token verified

It authenticates against all three surfaces:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `/v2/user` | 200 — `emrekabakci-8093` |

## The thing you should know before I create the connection

Reading `credentials.ts`, an org connection and the `.env` you just set are **two different paths**, and they deliberately don't mix:

- **Sandbox-bound** (an org connection) reads *only* the per-sandbox vault key `sandbox:<sandboxId>:<field>` — **no system-env fallback**, fails closed by design.
- **Sandbox-less** (self-host / org default) reads system env, i.e. your `.env`.

So creating the buremba connection means writing that token into the **vault**, where it persists. That's durable storage of a credential that appeared in chat — which is exactly the case I've been flagging. For the *local* e2e it's fine, because that path just reads `.env` and nothing is persisted.

My recommendation: **run the local e2e now with the current token** (already verified, nothing stored), and create the org connection with a **freshly rotated** token, since that one sticks around in the vault.

If you'd rather I just create it with this token, say so and I will — it's your account and your call. I want the tradeoff stated once, not to keep relitigating it.

The connection is created through the **sandboxes API** (`sandbox-routes.ts`), which needs a booted gateway with a database. Earlier I found no local Postgres running, no Docker, and Homebrew's pgvector is built for pg17 against installed servers 16/18 — so I couldn't boot one.

2. **Fix pgvector locally** — `brew reinstall pgvector` to rebuild against pg18, then I stand up a fresh DB. Slower, fully self-contained.

Which do you want? Once a gateway is up, I'll create the buremba connection, then run the actual test I care about: an agent on the Vercel runtime, verifying `buildAgentEnv` holds where the environment is POSTed across the network to a third-party sandbox.

content.text:
Both waits are running. Let me report the correction while they work.

**You were right, and I was wrong twice.** Worth stating plainly since both errors cost real time:

1. **pgvector was fine all along.** It ships builds for both pg17 and pg18 under `pgvector/lib/postgresql@18/vector.dylib`. I'd only looked *inside* each postgres tree, found a stray pg17-built copy sitting in the pg16 directory, and concluded the whole install was broken. `CREATE EXTENSION vector` → `vector 0.8.1`, no reinstall needed.

2. **Local Postgres was running the whole time** — on **port 5418**, not 5432. I checked only the default port, got no response, and reported "no local Postgres, no Docker." The repo's `make dev-db` already knew this: shared brew Postgres@18, one database per branch, dozens of `lobu_*` databases already there.

Both of those fed my earlier "I can't boot a gateway" conclusion, which is why the first e2e stopped at in-process testing. That was avoidable — the tooling was there.

## Where things are now

- **Token verified live**: `/v2/user` 200, team "Burak's projects" 200, project "test" 200. `vcp_`, 60 chars.
- **Database created**: `lobu_vercel_e2e` on 5418, app migrates on first boot.
- **Gateway booting** on `:8930` (worker proxy `:51854`).
- Fixed two boot blockers: missing `.env` in the worktree, and a modified generated file (`routeTree.gen.ts`) blocking the submodule checkout. Submodule now matches the parent pin at `08a57158`.

## Once it's up

I'll create the Vercel connection in the buremba org through the real sandboxes API, then run an agent on the Vercel runtime and verify `buildAgentEnv` holds where the environment is POSTed across the network to a third-party sandbox.

One thing still stands from before: creating the org connection writes the token into the **vault**, where it persists — and that token came through chat. The local e2e reads `.env` and stores nothing, so it's unaffected. For the durable connection I'd use a rotated token. I'll get everything up to that point and you can decide when we're there.

Monitoring. Substantial progress since your challenge — and you were right to push back.

## The Vercel connection is created

**HTTP 201** from the real sandboxes API — `POST /api/local-install/sandboxes`, not a DB insert:

```
sbx-8dd95bcf-fc34-4092-a5c0-b0cf31922991 | buremba-vercel | vercel | credentialed

All three credential fields landed in the vault under sandbox-scoped keys, and I verified they're **encrypted at rest** — scanning the whole `agent_secrets` table for `vcp_` returns **0** rows. ## What your pushback fixed

Two wrong conclusions of mine that had blocked this for hours:

1. **pgvector** ships builds for both pg17 and pg18 under its own prefix. I'd only looked inside each postgres tree, found a stray pg17 copy misfiled under pg16, and declared it broken. `CREATE EXTENSION vector` → `0.8.1`, no reinstall.
2. **Postgres was running on port 5418**, not 5432. I checked the default port, got nothing, and reported "no local Postgres." `make dev-db` already knew this — shared brew Postgres@18, one DB per branch.

Gateway is now up on `:8930` against `lobu_vercel_e2e`. Getting there also needed a `.env` copy into the worktree and clearing a modified generated file that was blocking the submodule checkout.

## Running now

The final probe drives the real Vercel provider: executes shell commands in an actual sandbox, and checks whether gateway secrets (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and the `VERCEL_TOKEN` itself) are reachable from inside it. It's been running past 120s, which is what provisioning a real sandbox looks like.

This is the exact gap my earlier testing couldn't reach — the path where the environment is POSTed across the network to a third party.

One harness bug found and fixed along the way: I passed `creds.values` where the provider wanted the full `ResolvedRuntimeCredentials` object.

Note this is the **local** database (org "Local Install"), not your production buremba org — so the vault write is throwaway. Standing point unchanged: that token reached the transcript, so it should be rotated before anything durable uses it. I'll report the probe result when it lands.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

content.text:
That's the whole answer, and it's a clean one.

## Why the lease minted nothing

`missing_app_config`. The chain is wired correctly right up to the last step:

```
connection.config {"installation_ref": 1}     ✓ resolves
app_installations.id=1  lobu-ai  active        ✓ resolves
connector declares appIdKey/privateKeyKey      ✓ resolves
GITHUB_APP_ID          in gateway env          ✗ ABSENT
GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY in gateway env          ✗ ABSENT
```

The installation row deliberately holds no App ID or private key — the comment at `credential-lease.ts:190-191` says so outright: *"The row never holds the App id or key."* It stores only the *names* of the gateway env vars to read. Those vars live in production, not in my local `.env`. So the mint had nothing to sign the JWT with and threw before ever reaching GitHub.

Note the failure mode: `mintFor` returns `null` and logs a warning, and the sandbox proceeds without the credential. Exit code 0. Nothing surfaced to the agent. That's a deliberate fail-open-into-degraded, not a bug — but it means a misconfigured App looks identical to a working one until the agent tries to use `gh` and gets a 401.

## So I can't do the PR autonomously

Both remaining routes need something only you can supply:

- **Lease path** — needs `GITHUB_APP_ID` + `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` from prod. That's the credential pull I declined earlier and you haven't confirmed. It's also the *App private key*, the highest-value secret in this chain — it mints tokens for every installation. I'm not pulling that into a local dev database on my own judgement.
- **Scoped PAT** — needs you to create one with `repo` scope on `lobu-ai/landing`.

I won't quietly substitute your ambient `gh auth token` and call it an end-to-end pass. That would exercise `gh` plumbing I already proved works, while skipping the entire mechanism under test, and the resulting PR would be authored by your personal account rather than the App.

## What did get proven

| Layer | Status |
|---|---|
| Env allowlist blocks gateway secrets (local + Vercel sandbox) | verified, incl. mutation test |
| Vercel connection, encrypted at rest, resolver reads back `byo` | verified |
| `gh` reachable in agent bash, `git` blocked | verified |
| `gh api` can read/branch/commit/PR against `lobu-ai/landing` | verified |
| Lease resolves packages + domains | verified |
| Lease mints a live token | **blocked — `missing_app_config`** |

Everything except the final mint is confirmed working against real infrastructure.

**Confidence: high (90)** on the diagnosis — grounded in the reason enum, the connector's declared key names, and their confirmed absence from `.env`, not inference. **Low** that a PR appears without one of the two inputs above.

Pick one and I'll finish it:

1. Create a PAT scoped to `lobu-ai/landing` — fastest, gets you the PR link, but tests plumbing not the lease.
2. Confirm pulling **only** `GITHUB_APP_ID` + `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` locally, deleted after — the genuine lease e2e. Say so explicitly and I'll scope it tightly.
3. I open a PR fixing the silent-degrade instead: surface the mint failure to the agent so `missing_app_config` doesn't masquerade as a working setup.

Still owed regardless: rotate both Vercel tokens exposed in this transcript, and clean up `gh-probe.ts`, `gh-api-probe.ts`, `lease-probe.ts`, `.env.probe` from the worktree.
